refs.quote: Administer PROTONIX For Delayed-Release Oral Suspension approximately 30 minutes prior to a meal via oral administration in apple juice or applesauce or nasogastric tube in apple juice only.

dose.frequency: once daily 30 minutes prior to a meal

regimens.dose_text: 40 mg once daily via >=16 French NG/G-tube using Delayed-Release Oral Suspension packet in apple juice only (10 mL apple juice flush x 3).

renal_basis.note: Section 12.3 states pharmacokinetic parameters in severe renal impairment are similar to healthy subjects; no CrCl cutoff specified.

hepatic.value: In mild to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A to C), AUC increases 5- to 7-fold (similar to CYP2C19 poor metabolizers) with minimal accumulation on once-daily dosing; no dosage adjustment warranted for 40 mg/day. Doses higher than 40 mg/day have not been studied in hepatically impaired patients.

refs.quote: Although serum half-life values increased to 7–9 hours and AUC values increased by 5- to 7-fold in hepatic-impaired patients, these increases were no greater than those observed in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers, where no dosage adjustment is warranted.
Pantoprazole is a PPI that suppresses the final step in gastric acid production by covalently binding to the (H + , K + )-ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell.

mg_safety.note: Proton pump inhibitor; no neuromuscular junction blocking warnings.

value.instructions: Do not split, chew, or crush Delayed-Release Tablets or Oral Suspension granules. For NG or G-tube (>=16 French), use 40 mg For Delayed-Release Oral Suspension packet with apple juice only: empty packet into 60 mL catheter-tip syringe barrel attached to tube, add 10 mL apple juice, gently tap/shake, and repeat rinse at least twice more with 10 mL apple juice.

refs.quote: Do not split, chew, or crush PROTONIX Delayed-Release Tablets and PROTONIX For Delayed-Release Oral Suspension.

Add 10 mL (2 teaspoonfuls) of apple juice and gently tap and/or shake the barrel of the syringe to help rinse the syringe and tube. Repeat at least twice more using the same amount of apple juice (10 mL or 2 teaspoonfuls) each time. No granules should remain in the syringe.

pgx.value: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers (~3% of Caucasians/African-Americans, 17% to 23% of Asians) have minimal accumulation (<=23%) with once-daily dosing; no dosage adjustment is needed in adults. Pediatric CYP2C19*2/*2 poor metabolizers exhibit >6-fold higher AUC and ~10-fold lower clearance; consider dose reduction in known pediatric poor metabolizers.

refs.quote: For adult patients who are CYP2C19 poor metabolizers, no dosage adjustment is needed. Similar to adults, pediatric patients who have the poor metabolizer genotype of CYP2C19 (CYP2C19 *2/*2) exhibited greater than a 6-fold increase in AUC compared to pediatric extensive (CYP2C19 *1/*1) and intermediate (CYP2C19 *1/*x) metabolizers.
For known pediatric poor metabolizers, a dose reduction should be considered.
Hepatobiliary Disorders: hepatocellular damage leading to jaundice and hepatic failure
Skin and Subcutaneous Tissue Disorders: severe dermatologic reactions (some fatal), including erythema multiforme, SJS/TEN, DRESS, AGEP, angioedema (Quincke's edema) and cutaneous lupus erythematosus
Metabolism and Nutritional Disorders: hypomagnesemia, hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hyponatremia
Psychiatric Disorders: hallucination, confusion, insomnia, somnolence

value: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (erythema multiforme, SJS/TEN, DRESS, AGEP)

Musculoskeletal Disorders: rhabdomyolysis, bone fracture

mechanism_of_action.value: Proton pump inhibitor that suppresses the final step in gastric acid production by covalently binding to the (H+, K+)-ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell, inhibiting both basal and stimulated acid secretion for >24 hours.

refs.quote: Pantoprazole is a PPI that suppresses the final step in gastric acid production by covalently binding to the (H + , K + )-ATPase enzyme system at the secretory surface of the gastric parietal cell.
The main metabolic pathway is demethylation, by CYP2C19, with subsequent sulfation; other metabolic pathways include oxidation by CYP3A4.

value.effect: Decreased exposure of rilpivirine may reduce antiviral effect and promote drug resistance.
value.management: Concomitant use with PROTONIX is contraindicated.

refs.quote: Rilpivirine-containing products: Concomitant use with PROTONIX is contraindicated [see Contraindications (4) ] .

value.effect: Decreased exposure of nelfinavir may reduce antiviral effect and promote resistance.

refs.quote: Nelfinavir: Avoid concomitant use with PROTONIX. See prescribing information for nelfinavir.

value.effect: Increased exposure of saquinavir may increase antiretroviral toxicity.
value.management: Monitor for potential saquinavir toxicities; see saquinavir prescribing information.

refs.quote: Saquinavir: See the prescribing information for saquinavir and monitor for potential saquinavir toxicities.

value.effect: Increased INR and prothrombin time, which may lead to abnormal bleeding and death.
value.management: Monitor INR and prothrombin time; dose adjustment of warfarin may be needed.

refs.quote: Monitor INR and prothrombin time. Dose adjustment of warfarin may be needed to maintain target INR range.

value.effect: No clinically important effect on exposure to active metabolite of clopidogrel or clopidogrel-induced platelet inhibition.
value.management: No dose adjustment of clopidogrel is necessary when administered with an approved dose of PROTONIX.

refs.quote: No dose adjustment of clopidogrel is necessary when administered with an approved dose of PROTONIX.

value.effect: May elevate and prolong serum concentrations of methotrexate and/or hydroxymethotrexate, possibly leading to methotrexate toxicities.
value.management: A temporary withdrawal of PROTONIX may be considered in some patients receiving high-dose methotrexate.

refs.quote: A temporary withdrawal of PROTONIX may be considered in some patients receiving high-dose methotrexate.

value.drug_or_class: Mycophenolate Mofetil (MMF) and Drugs Dependent on Gastric pH
value.effect: Pantoprazole reduces absorption of pH-dependent drugs (MMF active metabolite MPA Cmax -57% to -78%, AUC -27% to -45%).
value.management: Use PROTONIX with caution in transplant patients receiving MMF.

refs.quote: Use PROTONIX with caution in transplant patients receiving MMF. See the prescribing information for other drugs dependent on gastric pH for absorption.

tier.note: Published observational studies (ENTIS n=53, Denmark n=549, meta-analysis n=1,530) did not show an association with major malformations or adverse pregnancy outcomes, and organogenesis animal studies were negative up to 88x/16x human dose; however, pre/postnatal rat studies at 1-6x human dose showed pup mortality, decreased weight, and bone morphology changes, and label warns to advise pregnant women of potential fetal harm.

refs.quote: Available data from published observational studies did not demonstrate an association of major malformations or other adverse pregnancy outcomes with pantoprazole.
Advise pregnant women of the potential risk of fetal harm.

contraception.value: Does not reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy.
